To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
social bookmarking systems are a good model for social information retrieval.

(i) social bookmarking systems are a novel form of social network with a specific network structure, (ii) this network structure can be used to improve information retrieval, and (iii) this can be achieved by using the social network structure to create a new ranking algorithm that exploits the social network.

the following questions: (i) What structural properties characterize folksonomies? (ii) How does a folksonomy evolve over time? (iii) Can we predict the evolution of a folksonomy? (iv) How can we use the structure of a folksonomies for the exploration of resources and for the retrieval of relevant information?

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the folksonomy is a network that shows a high clustering coefficient, a low average path length and a power-law degree distribution, which are all characteristics of a scale-free network.
social bookmarking systems are not only useful for the individual users, but also for the community of users.
social information retrieval is not only possible, but also a very promising approach for the future.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are trying to understand and exploit the structure of social networks.
we have developed a novel method for social information retrieval based on the logfiles of social systems.
we are able to show that the folksonomy structure is a good indicator of quality and popularity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the structure of folksonomies is not random, but follows specific laws, and that these laws are related to the success of social information retrieval systems.
the tripartite hypergraphs of folksonomies are scale-free and show a power law degree distribution for all three types of nodes.
the structure of folksonomies has a profound impact on the retrieval performance of social information retrieval (SIR) systems.
